s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of generalized painful skin lesions and jaundice following a surgical procedure
salient_findings: Generalized painful fluid-filled skin lesions
Yellow scleral discoloration
Fever following removal of a tibial implant
Development of pruritus and fluid-filled rashes after antibiotic use
Icterus with elevated liver enzymes and bilirubin levels
key_facts: 22-year-old man
15-day history of generalized painful fluid-filled skin lesions
7 days of yellow scleral discoloration
1 month of fever following removal of a tibial implant
History of tibial fracture treated with internal fixation
Surgical-site infection and persistent fever after implant removal
Initial treatment with paracetamol without relief
Development of generalized pruritus after starting ciprofloxacin
Denial of angioedema, dyspnea, abdominal distention, lower-limb swelling, hematemesis, melena, altered sensorium, alcohol use, or immunocompromise
Afebrile with stable vital signs on examination
Icterus without pallor, clubbing, cyanosis, lymphadenopathy, or dehydration
Multiple generalized vesicles and bullae with non-hemorrhagic crusts on dermatologic examination
Mucosal findings including hemorrhagic lip crusts and penile erosion
Elevated leukocyte count with neutrophilia and eosinophilia
Abnormal liver function tests with elevated AST, ALT, and alkaline phosphatase
Elevated total bilirubin with conjugated hyperbilirubinemia

shortlist.label: Stevens-Johnson syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Acute onset of generalized painful skin lesions and jaundice following ciprofloxacin use

shortlist.label: DRESS syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Generalized pruritus, skin lesions, and systemic symptoms after starting ciprofloxacin

shortlist.label: Toxic epidermal necrolysis
shortlist.why_kept: Severe skin lesions and mucosal involvement following medication use

shortlist.label: Acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis
shortlist.why_kept: Widespread pustular rash and systemic symptoms after antibiotic use

shortlist.label: Drug-induced liver injury
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated liver enzymes and jaundice following ciprofloxacin use

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including generalized painful fluid-filled skin lesions, yellow scleral discoloration, fever, and elevated liver function tests, along with the development of generalized pruritus after starting ciprofloxacin, are consistent with DRESS syndrome, which is a severe cutaneous adverse reaction that can involve the skin, liver, and other organs.

rejected.label: Stevens-Johnson syndrome
rejected.why: While Stevens-Johnson syndrome is a severe cutaneous adverse reaction, it typically involves the mucous membranes more prominently and has a higher mortality rate, which is not indicated in this case.

rejected.label: Toxic epidermal necrolysis
rejected.why: Toxic epidermal necrolysis is a more severe condition with widespread skin necrosis, which is not described in this patient's presentation.

rejected.label: Acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis
rejected.why: Acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis is characterized by numerous small, sterile pustules, which is not consistent with the patient's presentation of generalized vesicles and bullae.

rejected.label: Drug-induced liver injury
rejected.why: While the patient has abnormal liver function tests, the presence of skin lesions and other systemic symptoms suggests a more complex condition like DRESS syndrome rather than isolated drug-induced liver injury.
